note: Pathogenic biallelic SNUPN variants directly cause spinocerebellar ataxia and cerebellar atrophy via splicing defects in Purkinje cells, broadening the disease spectrum beyond isolated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.

evidence.text: Biallelic SNUPN variants were identified in families with spinocerebellar atrophy, and knock-in mouse models demonstrated cerebellar ataxia, cerebellar atrophy, and Purkinje cell splicing defects, indicating cerebellar pathology is an intrinsic feature of SNUPN dysfunction.

source.title: SNUPN variants cause spinocerebellar atrophy by disrupting global splicing in cerebellar Purkinje cells
source.quote: Mutations in the SNUPN gene... have recently been implicated in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy... We identified pathogenic variants in the SNUPN gene in two families with spinocerebellar atrophy... These results expand the clinical spectrum of SNUPN-related disorders beyond skeletal muscle and highlight splicing dysregulation as a potential mechanism underlying cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.text: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy encompasses phenotypes ranging from pure muscular dystrophy to complex multi-system manifestations including spinocerebellar ataxia, neurodevelopmental symptoms, and asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia... One patient presented with asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy.
